claim: Instance types combine CPU, memory, storage and networking capacity in different ways, and each instance type includes one or more instance sizes, so you can scale resources to the requirements of the workload.
question: Why does an instance type come in several sizes?

values.spoken: each type comes in several sizes

values.display: scale your resources to the requirements
values.spoken: pick the size that fits the workload

evidence.quote: Instance types comprise varying combinations of CPU, memory, storage, and networking capacity and give you the flexibility to choose the appropriate mix of resources for your applications. Each instance type includes one or more instance sizes, allowing you to scale your resources to the requirements of your target workload.

claim: AWS can schedule events to reboot, stop or retire your instances and notifies you in advance by email; an affected instance in an Auto Scaling group is eventually replaced by Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling as part of its health checks.
question: What does AWS do before a scheduled event affects an instance, and what happens to an instance in an Auto Scaling group?

values.display: schedule events to reboot, stop, and retire
values.spoken: AWS can schedule reboot, stop and retire events

values.display: AWS notifies you in advance by email
Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling eventually replaces it

evidence.quote: To ensure infrastructure reliability and performance, AWS can schedule events to reboot, stop, and retire your instances.
If one of your instances will be affected by a scheduled event, AWS notifies you in advance by email, using the email address that's associated with your AWS account.

When an instance is affected by a scheduled event, and it is part of an Auto Scaling group, Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling eventually replaces it as part of its health checks, with no further action necessary on your part.
